findings.claim: ADR-0003 has no layer for the kept v1 unit tests. Item 1 says 'Two layers, and nothing else' and item 4 says 'No algorithm gets its own test entry point'. The owner decided v1 unit tests stay and v2 is built until the tests of kept parts pass. 136 of 210 v1 tests import ../src/, so they only pass if v2 keeps compatible src module paths and exports. The ADR names no KEEP-PASS set and no src API contract.
findings.evidence: ADR-0003:22 'Two layers, and nothing else'; :29 'No algorithm gets its own test entry point'; cm-main: grep -lE "from ['\"](../)+src" tests/**/*.test.* = 136 of 210; e.g. tests/store.test.ts, tests/truncate.test.ts, tests/store-bytecap.test.ts import src directly.
findings.fix: Add a third layer 'v1-kept' to ADR-0003: a per-file list (KEEP-PASS / PORT / RETIRED with ADR id) and a rule that v2 keeps the src import paths those KEEP-PASS files use, or ports them with a reviewed diff. Gate v2.0 on KEEP-PASS green plus GP1-GP11.

findings.claim: Q9 fixes the runner as node:test against built .mjs. The v1 tests run on vitest with TypeScript sources. Keeping v1 tests means vitest (and its TS transform) must stay in v2 devDependencies and CI; the spec never says so.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:415 'Test runner = node:test'; :258 'no transform step is needed'; cm-main package.json:94 "test": "vitest run", :120 "vitest": "^4.0.18"; vitest.config.ts:7 include tests/**/*.test.ts.
findings.fix: State two runners: vitest for tests/ (v1 kept) and node:test for e2e/. Add both to the CI matrix and to the 10-minute budget.

findings.claim: The /release skill runs only 'node --test e2e/cases'. It never runs the kept v1 tests, so a release can ship while a KEEP-PASS v1 test fails.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md:9 'Run the deterministic tests: npm ci && npm run build && node --test e2e/cases'. ADR-0013:35 ci job = 'GP1-GP11' only.
findings.fix: Add 'npx vitest run <KEEP-PASS list>' to step 2 and to the ci job in ADR-0013; stop on any failure.

findings.claim: 'B rows (124) ... Each becomes a GP case assertion' has no mapping. Only 53 of the 124 B issue ids appear anywhere in TECH-SPEC or the ADRs; the issue map has no GP column (0 GP refs). 71 B items have no named E2E case, so 'E2E coverage of every B item' is not checkable.
findings.evidence: Command: B ids from tickets/v2-issue-map.md (class column = B) = 124 unique; grep of '#<id>' in TECH-SPEC.md + adr/*.md hits 53. grep -c 'GP[0-9]' tickets/v2-issue-map.md = 0. TECH-SPEC §6.2 'Requirement ids (examples)'.
findings.fix: Add a 'GP case' column to every B and M row in v2-issue-map.md (GPn/<case> or LIVE/<case>), plus a CI script that fails when a B row has no case or the case file does not exist.

findings.claim: The harness '--cases routing,deny,compact,hooks' has no case for the live checks other ADRs assign to it: ADR-0016 LV8, LV9, LV10 (subagent large-output, a MUST) and ADR-0008 LV1, LV2. ADR-0016 says 'Live checks (ADR-0012 harness)' but ADR-0012 does not list them, and the release skill runs only '--models haiku' default cases.
findings.evidence: ADR-0012:26 '--cases routing,deny,compact,hooks'; :48-52 case list; ADR-0016:45-53 'Live checks (ADR-0012 harness)' LV8, LV9, LV10, LV1, LV2; SKILL.md:10 'node e2e/live/run.mjs --models haiku'.
findings.fix: Add a 'subagent' case (LV8-LV10) and an 'updated-io' case (LV1, LV2) to ADR-0012 and make them default cases, so /release runs them.

findings.claim: GS3 needs G25 answered for Copilot CLI, ZCode, Pi and OpenCode 2. ADR-0012 runs hook firing (G25) only on installed agents, which are claude and codex; the four GS3 agents are SKIPPED. GS3 can never pass, and GS2 is rewritten only for routing.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:36 GS3 'do hooks fire for MCP tools on Copilot CLI, ZCode, Pi and OpenCode 2'; ADR-0012:17 'only claude and codex. The others are not installed and print SKIPPED'; :60 rewrites GS2 only.
findings.fix: Either rewrite GS3 like GS2 (answered per agent or SKIPPED with reason, with a source-code citation as the fallback answer) or add install steps for those four CLIs to the harness.

findings.claim: GP9 asserts stdin EOF exit but not the non-TTY gate. v1 tests/server-stdin-eof-exit.test.ts pins that the 'end' listener is NOT registered when stdin is a TTY (OpenCode ts-plugin path). If that file is retired and GP9 only checks EOF exit, v2 can re-break #534/#236.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:295 GP9 'stdin EOF, parent kill ... exit < 2 s' (no TTY case). cm-main tests/server-stdin-eof-exit.test.ts:42 'lifecycle.ts gates the end listener on !isTTY', :95 isTTY true case. Ledger rows 236, 534 suggest GP9.
findings.fix: Mark server-stdin-eof-exit.test.ts and lifecycle.test.ts KEEP-PASS, or add GP9 cases 'stdin is TTY: no exit on EOF' and 'stdin is a pipe: exit on EOF'.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 939c5ca8 2026-03-13 'fix: add process lifecycle guard to prevent orphaned MCP servers (#103)'; test d56a9fc0 2026-05-12 'test(lifecycle): pin stdin EOF recheck contract behind #534'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'The end listener wired in lifecycle.ts (added in #388) is load-bearing for the #534 fix ... adds four pinning tests so future refactors can not silently undo the recovery path. Tests cover: end listener registered when stdin is not a TTY, NOT registered when stdin is a TTY (OpenCode ts-plugin path)'. Later edits c5e0fbc0 (#833), 77e22a46 (#854/#855). REGRESSION_RISK: orphaned servers at 100% CPU (#534) or spurious -32000 Connection closed (#236). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the TTY gate; test both TTY and pipe stdin.

findings.claim: Item 4 lists 'truncation' as a pure algorithm v2 keeps and tests. Owner decision: no truncation as a decision or reduction mechanism. v1 tests/truncate.test.ts cannot be KEEP-PASS for a part v2 drops.
findings.evidence: ADR-0003:29 '(chunker, ranking, gitignore matching, truncation)'; cm-main tests/truncate.test.ts imports src.
findings.fix: Drop 'truncation' from item 4; mark truncate.test.ts RETIRED with the ADR that removes it (code-point-safe output cut in GP4 stays as a boundary check).

findings.claim: PRD says 'One formula, one unit test' for stats savings, while TECH-SPEC puts it in GP10 (E2E) and does not mark this PRD line as superseded.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:147 'One formula, one unit test'; TECH-SPEC.md:297 GP10 'saved = sandbox bytes - returned bytes'; superseded table TECH-SPEC.md:52-58 lacks it.
findings.fix: Add the line to the superseded table, or keep it as a KEEP-PASS unit test under the new ADR-0003 layer.

findings.claim: Default run is Haiku only, and /release uses the default. TECH-SPEC §6.5 thresholds are 'per model' over Opus, Sonnet and Haiku, and the ADR-0006 alwaysLoad A/B is 'before every release'. Neither the A/B nor Sonnet/Opus runs happen in a release.
findings.evidence: ADR-0012:56 'Default run. Haiku on Claude Code'; TECH-SPEC.md:323 'Opus, Sonnet and Haiku', :328 'thresholds ... per model', :329 'A/B tested here before every release'; SKILL.md:10 '--models haiku'.
findings.fix: Either state that release gates on Haiku only and run all models by hand on a stated cadence, or make the A/B and the 3-model run a named harness case.
